module_summary: filer_copy.c is the classic paste engine: recursive copy() of files and folders, PSU backup and restore, the Move manifest that deletes sources only after every copy was verified (filerMoveFinish), copy diagnostics, save-title extraction (filerGetGameTitle) and MC/VMC/XFROM attribute restoration. filer_device.c decides whether two devices can be used together and loads their IOP driver stacks before a transfer. filer_fileops.c wraps fileXio (open, stat, rename-no-replace, remove, mkdir, lseek, read/write) with host:/cf:/mc1: path mapping and mc/FatFs error normalisation; filer_mount.c manages the four pfsN: mount slots for HDD partitions. ftp_session.c polls the ps2ftpd IOP module over SIF RPC with 1 s timeouts; gui.c holds the classic ynDialog/nonDialog/keyboard widgets, which the dashboard replaces through function-pointer overrides while it is active.

findings.title: copy() allocates a second 1 MiB buffer (buff2) that never overlaps any I/O
findings.problem: For a file of at least 1 MiB on the fast-device path, copy() allocates buff2 (another COPY_BUFFER_FAST_DEFAULT, 1 MiB) and alternates the two buffers per chunk. Each chunk is one read and then one write of the same buffer (copyChunkIo, filer_copy.c:67-76), and DashFileTransferChunk waits until the worker job is done (dash_ui.c:1463-1464) or the chunk runs inline (line 1563). No read ever overlaps a write, so the second buffer only doubles the peak heap.
findings.fix: Delete buff2, buffCount, buffIndex and copyBuff, and pass buff to the chunk.
findings.benefit: 1 MiB less peak heap during every fast-path copy of a file >= 1 MiB (0x100000, filer_copy.c:32; INFERRED); about 14 lines removed.
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:58-83 (copyChunkIo reads into c->buf, then writes the same c->buf), 1398-1436, 1557-1565, 1588-1592, 1696-1700; dash_ui.c:1452-1466 (dashWorkerSubmit, then while (!dashWorkerDone(id)) loadingDraw()). Grep for buff2 over src/Launchstation/src and include: only filer_copy.c. buffSize equals COPY_BUFFER_FAST_DEFAULT only when copyBufferSize (filer_copy.c:90-117) picks the 1 MiB default and the file is at least that large (hdd, smb, udpfs, mmce, ata, ilink, cdfs sources and destinations); a PSU restore can also reach it through psu_restore_buff.

findings.title: Recursive copy() keeps a full 2048-entry listing (896 KB) at every folder level
findings.problem: Each folder level memaligns MAX_ENTRY FILEINFOs (2048 x 448 B = 896 KB) for its listing and holds it while all its subfolders are copied, so a tree d levels deep holds d x 896 KB of listings although a typical folder has a few dozen entries. copy() allows 15 nested levels (MAX_RECURSE 16), about 13 MB. getFileSize() and delete() repeat the same per-level allocation.
findings.fix: List into one MAX_ENTRY scratch buffer shared by all levels (getDirComplete writes it only before the children run and again after they return), then memalign only nfiles entries for the level and copy them; do the second listing at line 1179 into the scratch and compare it with the level's copy. getFileSize() can use the same scratch.
findings.justification: A 5-level copy holds about 4.4 MB of mostly empty listings out of a heap of about 25 MB (evidence/Launchstation/BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:207), on top of up to 2 MiB of copy buffers, and deeper trees approach 13 MB and can fail with -ENOMEM. One shared scratch keeps the peak at 896 KB plus the entries really listed, for about 6 more lines.
findings.benefit: Peak heap of a d-level copy drops from d x 917,504 B to 917,504 B plus the used entries (INFERRED: FILEINFO 256 + 66 + 64-byte-aligned 64-byte stats = 448 B, x MAX_ENTRY 2048).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:742-760 (comment: MAX_ENTRY entries are about 900 KB), 911-935, 1122-1192; files[] is read inside the child loop (1163-1164) and overwritten by the second listing only after it (1179). MAX_ENTRY 2048 (launchelf.h:205); FILEINFO layout launchelf.h:560-565, sceMcTblGetDir 64 bytes aligned 64 as mirrored in tests/test_copy_psu_listing.py:104-106. MAX_RECURSE 16 (include/filer_shared.h:40), refusal at recurses + 1 >= MAX_RECURSE (filer_copy.c:797). compile.yml:383-386 also states each level's listing is about 900 KB. filer_actions.c:310-311 (getFileSize) and 1981-1984 (delete) allocate the same per level. INFERRED part: the heap size (BUILD-EVIDENCE.md:207 estimate) and that deep copies run short.

findings.title: copy() and filerGetGameTitle() join paths into 1025-byte stack buffers with sprintf/strcat and no length check
findings.problem: Each recursion level builds in, out and tmp (char[MAX_PATH], 1025) as the parent path plus a listed name with sprintf, and filerGetGameTitle builds dir and tmpdir with strcpy/strcat (path + name + '/' + name for the PS1 probe). Names come from listings (FAT, exFAT and SMB allow 255 chars; FILEINFO.name is 256) and nothing bounds the total, so a source tree whose path passes about 770 chars (four nested 190-char folder names) overflows copy()'s stack buffers on the UI thread, and long names overflow tmpdir on the worker when the browser lists titles. delete() and getFileSize() bound the same joins with snprintf and return -ENAMETOOLONG.
findings.fix: At copy() entry, after newfile is set, return copyDiagFail(-ENAMETOOLONG) when strlen(inPath) + strlen(file.name) + 2 or strlen(outPath) + strlen(newfile.name) + 2 (plus room for the PSU name suffix in PSU backup mode) exceeds MAX_PATH. In filerGetGameTitle build dir and tmpdir with snprintf and return -1 when they do not fit.
findings.justification: A stack overflow (crash or silent corruption, EE threads have no stack protector) on input a user can have: deep trees with long names. One bound check at copy() entry covers all five joins, the same pattern delete()/getFileSize() already use.
findings.benefit: Closes a stack overflow on long paths; about 4 lines added (READ).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:560-682 and 752-1300. MAX_NAME 256, MAX_PATH 1025 (launchelf.h:201-205); FILEINFO.name[MAX_NAME] (launchelf.h:562). Child levels receive the parent's in/out as inPath/outPath (filer_copy.c:1117-1118, 1133, 1164), so each level adds a name and a slash. moveRecord checks its own join (filer_copy.c:180) but runs after the sprintf at 849. filer_actions.c:314-317 (getFileSize) and 1972-1973 (delete) bound the same joins with snprintf. filerGetGameTitle runs on the worker for browser listings (dash_browser.c:321) and from copy() (filer_copy.c:949, 1050). Confidence Med: needs unusually long names.

findings.title: Cancelling the name prompt of Paste-with-rename still pastes under the original name and replaces a same-named file
findings.problem: With PasteMode PM_RENAME, copy() asks for a new name; when keyboard() returns -1 (cancel, which classicKeyboard returns when the dashboard keyboard is dismissed) it copies the original name back and carries on. For a file the destination is then removed and recreated without a prompt (genRemove and O_TRUNC at 1382-1383), so cancelling the rename the user chose to avoid a name clash overwrites the existing destination file, and a Move completes under the original name.
findings.fix: When keyboard() returns a negative value, return COPY_KEPT_DESTINATION (nothing written, nothing for a Move to delete) instead of reverting to the original name; keep the revert only for an empty name.
findings.justification: Replaces the fallback branch with an early return; today a cancelled prompt silently overwrites user data.
findings.benefit: A cancelled rename no longer overwrites a destination file (READ); no size change.
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:816-823 (keyboard(newfile.name, 36) <= 0 -> strcpy(newfile.name, file.name)), 873 (out built from newfile.name), 1374-1391 (genRemove(out), then genOpen with O_TRUNC|O_CREAT, no prompt; folders instead get the newdir -17 prompt at 1049-1074). gui.c:144-262 keyboard returns -1 on cancel; dash_widgets.c:663-668 classicKeyboard returns -1 when dashModalKeyboard fails. Dashboard Paste-rename reaches it through opPaste -> filerPasteModeInto(..., rename) (dash_browser.c:894, filer_browser.c:2321-2324). subfunc_Paste treats COPY_KEPT_DESTINATION as kept (filer_browser.c:2214-2216).

findings.title: copy() re-prepares both device stacks for every nested file and folder; on host: each call costs 2-3 PC round trips
findings.problem: subfunc_Paste prepares the source and destination stacks once (filer_browser.c:2164), yet copy() calls prepareTransferDeviceStacks again at every recursion level, once per copied file and folder. For host: that runs initHOST(), which opens host:elflist.txt and, when it is absent, opens and closes the host: directory: 2-3 blocking network requests per entry on the UI thread, and a transient failure there aborts the copy midway. getFileSize() and delete() call ensurePathDeviceStackReady per entry the same way.
findings.fix: Call prepareTransferDeviceStacks in copy() only when recurses == 0 (once per clipboard item); nested levels use the same two devices. getFileSize() and delete() can leave the check to their top-level callers.
findings.benefit: Removes 2-3 host: requests per nested entry: a 1000-file host: copy saves about 2000-3000 requests, seconds of UI-thread time (INFERRED at ~1 ms per LAN round trip); other devices only save flag checks.
findings.evidence: Read filer_device.c:105-228: for host: ensurePathDeviceStackReady calls initHOST(); other devices are flag checks (loadHddModules init.c:2663-2670, isSmbDriverLoaded init.c:998-1002, loadUsbModules init.c:1740-1757). filer.c:1720-1737: initHOST = load_ps2host + fileXioOpen(host:elflist.txt), else fileXioDopen/Dclose(host:). The only level-0 caller of copy() is subfunc_Paste (filer_browser.c:2208), which already called prepareTransferDeviceStacks at 2164. Child levels pass the parent's in/out, same device prefixes (filer_copy.c:1117-1118). copy() runs on the UI thread (opPaste, dash_browser.c:877-894). readHOST also calls initHOST per listing (filer.c:1747), twice per copied folder.

findings.title: filerGetGameTitle leaves two bytes of a rejected PS1 header in the title, and copy() uses them for the .psu name
findings.problem: The PS1 probe reads the first 2 bytes of the candidate save straight into out and returns -1 when they are not SC, leaving those bytes (and stale bytes after them) in out. The browser callers clear the title on failure, but copy() runs transcpy_sjis on the title whatever the result: a PSU backup with titles shown (or PSU_HugeNames) of a folder that holds a same-named, 8 KB-multiple file that is no PS1 save is named after those bytes, and the folder-conflict prompt shows them as the save title.
findings.fix: Read the 2-byte magic into a local buffer (or clear out[0] at finish when ret < 0) so a failed lookup always leaves an empty title.
findings.benefit: Correct .psu name and prompt in that case; no size change (READ).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:560-682: out[0] = 0 at 569, genRead(fd, out, 2) at 653, strncmp(out, SC) failure goes to finish at 655, finish does not clear out. Callers: dash_browser.c:321-322 and filer.c:2477-2479 reset title[0] on ret < 0; filer_copy.c:949-954 calls transcpy_sjis(cp, file.title) after any return, and 1050-1051 transcpy_sjis(tmp, newfile.title) likewise. np[0] is non-empty in that case, so the revert at 959-960 does not apply.

findings.title: filerGetGameTitle's .psu scan turns a large entry size into a backward seek and can loop up to 2^31 times
findings.problem: psu_pad_pos is an int computed from the u32 entry size read from the file, so a size of 0x80000000 or more becomes a negative SEEK_CUR offset that moves back to an earlier header, and the loop is bounded only by the first header's count (also from the file, up to 0x7FFFFFFF). A malformed .psu keeps the title scan re-reading the same headers, stalling the browser listing job on the worker (dash_browser.c:321) or the classic listing (filer.c:2477) whenever titles are shown.
findings.fix: Declare psu_pad_pos as u32 so the seek always goes forward; a bogus size then seeks past the end and the next header read fails.
findings.benefit: Removes a hang on malformed .psu files; no size change (READ; the trigger needs a crafted or corrupt file).
findings.evidence: Read filer_copy.c:560-628. psu_header.size is u32 (include/psu_types.h:32); PSU_content = PSU_head.size (613) bounds the loop; psu_pad_pos = (size + 0x3FF) & -0x400 (622) is stored in int (565) and passed to genLseek(fd, psu_pad_pos, SEEK_CUR) (623), whose offset is s64 (filer_fileops.c:680). Example: header 2 with size 0xFFFFFC00 gives -1024 and returns to header 1 at offset 512 every pass. The restore path checks entries against the file size first (psu_restore_check_entries, filer_copy.c:1024); this title path does not.
